newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Manuel sees rate knock-on from firm bonds.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Manuel sees rate knock-on from firm bonds.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said on Wednesday the strong performance of long bonds like the R150 could be a factor in the level of interest rates.
Manuel, addressing a news conference after the regular weekly cabinet meeting, was asked what his current thinking was on the level of interest rates.
"There's been a surge of interest (in long bonds) in the last few weeks," he replied.
"Certainly, we've seen a remarkable recovery. That's the kind of issue that makes a lot of difference to your borrowing strategy," he said.

"Clearly once that starts happening it feeds through the market generally. The interest rates, the bank rates are often a consequence of a hell of a lot of things that happened before, they're never stand-alone issues that you capriciously take decisins on.
"But it's a factor of flows and demand for South African government stock," he said.
The benchmark R150 issue is currently trading at its firmest level since September last year at around 15.10 percent.
